name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,586

clue.text: Animal trade's underhand dealings

blocks.note: a monkey is an animal
trade and business are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone running a shady trade in exotic animals is up to no good.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for mischievous or dishonest behaviour covers sly, underhand dealings in general.

clue.text: Admits going around briefly before getting joint right of possession

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
the first word goes around the next piece, enclosing it
getting means the following piece is added on at the end

blocks.note: to own up is to admit, so owns means admits
ere is an old word for before
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A legal account of how someone came to hold property through admissions and a share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as shared ownership, which suits the surface, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal title to a thing is the formal right of holding property, which is what owning it means.

clue.text: Russian peasant finding success in short supply by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to go by how the words are pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: a coup is a success, said like coo, and lack is a short supply

explanation.surface: A poor Russian farmer rarely has any luck or good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: COUP is French-derived and its P is silent, so it is spoken like coo.
explanation.definitionFit: Kulaks were relatively prosperous farmers in late Tsarist and early Soviet Russia, targeted by Stalin.

clue.text: Standard used for comparison of 100 arty kids reviewed

indicators.note: to review is to look again and revise, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hundred creative children have their work assessed against a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring rod a yard long gives its name to any benchmark that other things are judged against.

clue.text: Remove cover from explosive device found by peacekeepers

indicators.note: found by places the device beside the following piece, here after it

blocks.note: United Nations troops serve as peacekeepers
a percussion cap is a small explosive device

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping soldiers discover a bomb and must take its casing off.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap something is to take off its lid or top, removing its covering.

clue.text: Liam regularly beaten and shut up

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter in a steady pattern

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of the name
pounded means hit repeatedly, beaten

explanation.surface: Liam was routinely beaten up and locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Impounded means confined or locked in a pound, as with seized cars or stray animals.

clue.text: Letters from Frederic Austin's girl

indicators.note: letters from means a run of consecutive letters taken out of the following words

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: Correspondence from one Frederic Austin to his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederic Austin was an English singer and composer, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name, and crosswords often define names simply as boy or girl.

clue.text: Not hypocritical with regard to seeing that earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the phrase it follows first, ahead of the other piece

blocks.note: since and seeing that both mean because
re is the Latin-derived word for concerning

explanation.surface: A remark about honesty, phrased like a clause from a formal letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person means what they say, the opposite of a hypocrite who pretends.

clue.text: Plant spies to trap Wally

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: the CIA is the American spy agency
a wally is British slang for a fool, as is ass

explanation.surface: Secret agents set up a sting to catch someone named Wally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb about planting agents, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is a genus of tropical plants, one of which yields a cinnamon-like bark.

clue.text: Set aside letter looking into article 50

indicators.note: looking into suggests peering inside, so one piece goes within the others

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A document about Article 50, the Brexit withdrawal clause, being put to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: Article 50 of the Lisbon Treaty was the clause Britain triggered to leave the EU; here article and 50 are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a law or marriage is to declare it void, setting it aside as if it never was.

clue.text: First class piece torn apart

indicators.note: something torn apart is broken up, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A top-quality item has been ripped to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' looks like praise, but in British schools Reception is the first class a child joins, at age four or five.
explanation.definitionFit: In English primary schools the opening year group, before Year One, is called by this name.

clue.text: Raids oddly neglected story to penetrate Dickens' character

indicators.note: neglecting the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones
to penetrate is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of the word
Bill Sikes is the villain of Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: A tale of thefts is woven into the life of a Dickens villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Military strikes are attacks on a target, so raids and strikes are synonymous nouns.

clue.text: Best time to get cover for winger

blocks.note: a plum job is the best one going
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Advice on the ideal moment to provide protection for a wide footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a sports player on the wing, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathers cover a bird's body, and a winger is a whimsical name for any flying creature.

clue.text: Pasty's burnt remains discovered by penniless writer

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, abbreviated as P, so that letter goes
discovered by places the first piece alongside, here before, the second

blocks.note: ash is what is left after burning
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A burnt Cornish pasty, found ruined by a starving author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the baked pie, but it is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a pale, colourless, unhealthy-looking complexion.

clue.text: Literary failure almost leads to row becoming worse

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to come to naught is a literary way to say fail
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A book that flops sparks a quarrel that gets ever more bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a child, behaving worse means being more badly behaved, the comparative of naughty.

clue.text: Direct current

blocks.note: first meaning: without anything in between
second meaning: happening now, present

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like an electrical term, direct current, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both nearest, with nothing intervening, and belonging to the present moment.

clue.text: People concerned with murder perhaps

blocks.note: mortals are human beings
in can mean involved or concerned with, as in being in trade

explanation.surface: Describes those involved in a killing, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave wrong such as killing is the gravest category of wrongdoing; murder is an example.

clue.text: Ornate altar base made from variety of gypsum

indicators.note: something ornate is elaborately reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorated church altar stands on a plinth carved from mineral stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine-grained white stone used for carving is a form of gypsum or calcite.

clue.text: Bird speaks and Curt almost freaks out

indicators.note: almost means falling short, so the name loses its final letter
to freak out is to go wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone talks, and a man called Curt nearly loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapsucker is a North American woodpecker that drills trees to feed on sap.

clue.text: Last of critics getting extremely excited after sauce served up is sweetened

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the next word is kept
extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters only
in a down clue, served up means the word is written upwards, back to front
after puts the pieces before it later in the answer than what follows

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
ragu is an Italian meat sauce for pasta
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A food critic gets thrilled because the sauce is sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has had sugar added has literally been made sweeter.

clue.text: Haggard to choose at random Quatermain's end

indicators.note: end means just the final letter of the name is used

blocks.note: to draw is to pick by lot
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: It reads as how Rider Haggard picked the fate of his hero Allan Quatermain.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard wrote the Allan Quatermain novels, so 'Haggard' looks like the author, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks tired and gaunt, which is what a haggard face looks like.

clue.text: Lower in number after noon

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the one that follows it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for noon
read as numb-er, something that numbs: ether is an old anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A figure has dropped since midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but it is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old adjective meaning situated below, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Clearly described heartless fellow stabbing German in charge

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed
stabbing means going into, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
Ralph is a man's name, any fellow
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A vivid report of a cruel man knifing a German official.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic account is vivid and explicit, giving every detail plainly.

clue.text: Serve the purpose of pretence for instance

blocks.note: putting on an act is pretending
as introduces an example, like for instance

explanation.surface: A note on how a show of make-believe can be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as something is to function in that role, doing its job.

clue.text: Thrash about in river

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone flails around in the water of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To cream an opponent is informal for beating them heavily, just like to thrash them.

clue.text: Legendary rock band oddly ignored by American books on the origins of alternative metal

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps the even ones
origins means the first letters of the following words
in an across clue, on means placed after what follows it

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of the word
the first letters of the two words
A is the abbreviation for American
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A famous rock group's albums get ignored by American fans of alt-metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legendary rock band' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'rock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was a mythical stone of impenetrable hardness, a rock found in legend.

clue.text: Distribute everything before coming back

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is turned around

blocks.note: all means everything
to means before in telling time, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: Hand out everything before returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or assign portions, which is distributing them.

clue.text: Remembers involving the Queen's servants

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: to retain a fact is to remember it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the members of the royal household staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Retainers are long-serving attendants of a noble household, an old word for servants.

clue.text: Flexible and carefree? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is taken away

blocks.note: blithe means happy and carefree

explanation.surface: Someone supple and relaxed, but perhaps only after warming up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithe body is supple and bends easily, so it is flexible.

clue.text: Biased policeman misconstrued racism in Conservative supporter

indicators.note: something misconstrued is wrongly put together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
taken as written
a Tory backs the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A prejudiced officer mistook racism within a Tory voter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a joining word, but its letters belong to the anagram along with RACISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating people unfairly on grounds of race or sex is discrimination, so a prejudiced act is described this way.
